title: Split WebGL visual acceptance into independently sharded Playwright cases

scope.subject: Release visual-test topology and failure isolation for Personal Universe

research_summary: The current suite already uses Playwright native sharding and a GitHub Actions matrix with workers=1 per runner, but each viewport is still one long serial visual journey. Reuse Playwright test-level sharding by splitting Galaxy, Search, Places, Personal Signal system/orbit and Hero-world evidence into independent tests. Keep viewport-heavy tablet/mobile smoke as separate cases so one slow WebGL journey does not hide or delay unrelated failures.

sources.finding: Playwright distributes individual tests across shards; with fullyParallel enabled, test-level granularity improves balancing and failure isolation.
Playwright recommends workers=1 on CI for stability and scaling across machines with sharding rather than increasing workers on one runner.
GitHub Actions matrix jobs provide separate hosted runners and independent job/artifact failures.

search_ladder.conclusion: No broader visual-regression service is needed because the repository already has screenshots, traces, HTML reports and cloud runners; replacing that stack would add a vendor without fixing the monolithic test shape.
Playwright Test already supplies independent tests, retries/traces/screenshots and native sharding; split the visual journey at the test level instead of building a custom visual runner.
Existing Playwright sharding plus the GitHub Actions matrix already provides the required cross-runner parallelism while retaining workers=1.
No new helper dependency is needed; small shared setup/screenshot helpers inside the existing spec are sufficient.

candidates.name: Independent Playwright visual cases
candidates.reason: Turns each visual state into an independently failing test while preserving existing screenshots, traces, runtime hooks and CI reporting.

candidates.name: Playwright native sharding on GitHub matrix runners
candidates.reason: Already deployed and proven; finer test granularity lets the existing shards balance the visual workload without extra workers.

candidates.name: Multiple WebGL workers on one runner
candidates.reason: Would increase SwiftShader/WebGL contention and conflicts with the established one-worker-per-runner stability policy.

coverage_matrix.decision: Split each major visual state into its own Playwright test.

coverage_matrix.capability: Reduce slow-case blast radius and wall clock
coverage_matrix.decision: Let native sharding distribute the smaller tests across separate runners.

coverage_matrix.capability: Preserve one WebGL worker per runner
coverage_matrix.decision: Keep workers=1; do not add same-runner browser concurrency.

decision.rationale: Keep the existing Playwright + GitHub Actions stack and change only the test granularity. Independent visual cases gain isolated screenshots/traces and allow native sharding to balance slow WebGL work without longer timeouts or more workers per runner.
decision.fallback: If one scene remains intrinsically slow, isolate only that scene into its own test/project while keeping the same runtime assertions and one-worker-per-runner rule.
